title: Optimal T-Count for Block Encodings of Fermionic and Spin Hamiltonians
authors: Jiaxin Ma, Kevin J. Joven, Yuan Liu
abstract: We determine the non-Clifford $T$-gate cost of constructing block encodings of structured fermionic and spin Hamiltonians in a unitary Clifford$+T$ model, when arbitrarily many clean ancillas and unrestricted block-encoding subnormalization are allowed, but without mid-circuit measurements or classical feed-forward. Our main technical tool is an ancilla-compression theorem: any block encoding of an $n$-qubit operator with $a$ clean ancillas and at most $s$ $T$ gates can be compressed to use at most $\min\{a,n+2s\}$ ancillas, without increasing the absolute error or $T$-count. For general second-quantized Hamiltonians with bounded one- and two-body coefficients, at operator-norm block-encoding error $ε$, a volume-covering argument combined with circuit counting gives the worst-case lower bound $Ω(n^2\sqrt{\log(n^4/ε)})$, matching the existing upper bound at fixed precision. For the bond-dependent Kitaev honeycomb family on $n$ spins, we obtain independent lower bounds $Ω(n)$ from stabilizer nullity and $Ω(\log(1/ε))$ from one-qubit state preparation, established using different Hamiltonian instances. Together with an explicit LCU construction, they give the tight worst-case scaling $Θ(n+\log(1/ε))$. As an application, we evaluate the $T$-count of a Hamiltonian simulation circuit based on quantum singular value transformation, with each block-encoding query compiled separately. When phase synthesis and controlled queries add at most constant-factor overhead, the simulation $T$-count scales as the query count times the optimal $T$-count per query.
summary: This paper establishes the theoretical lower bounds on the T-gate count needed to encode and simulate complex fermionic and spin Hamiltonians using block encodings in a Clifford+T quantum circuit model. By developing advanced geometric and combinatorial arguments, the authors provide tight scaling laws for the required quantum resources. This research is crucial for understanding the computational cost limitations of simulating quantum matter on near-term quantum hardware.
main_problem: The paper determines the minimum T-gate count required to construct block encodings of structured fermionic and spin Hamiltonians within a unitary Clifford+T quantum circuit model.
main_result: For general fermionic Hamiltonians, the worst-case T-count scales as $\Theta(n^2 \log(n^4/\epsilon))$, while for Kitaev honeycomb spin Hamiltonians, the scaling is $\Theta(n + \log(1/\epsilon))$.
method: The authors employ volume-covering arguments and circuit counting techniques, alongside an ancilla-compression theorem, to establish rigorous lower bounds on the required T-gate resources.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on simulating fermionic and spin Hamiltonians (like the Kitaev model) using block encodings within a unitary Clifford+T circuit model, avoiding mid-circuit measurements.
key_observables: T-count (non-Clifford gate cost), block-encoding error ($\epsilon$), and the system size ($n$).
important_parameters: The scaling depends critically on the system size $n$ and the desired precision $\epsilon$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ability to use clean ancillas and that the simulation is performed in the unitary Clifford+T model without classical feed-forward.
paper_structure: The paper develops theoretical tools, including an ancilla-compression theorem, to derive lower bounds for the T-count complexity of encoding Hamiltonians, applying these bounds separately to fermionic and spin systems, and concluding with an application to QSVT.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental complexity bounds for simulating quantum many-body systems using near-term quantum hardware models (Clifford+T), directly impacting the feasibility assessment of quantum simulation algorithms.
